claim: The guest reports that one long running chat produced worse outcomes, while starting a new chat restored useful behavior.
note: This is a personal observation, not a controlled comparison.

claim: The Ralph pattern runs a coding agent repeatedly with the same small outer loop and prompt.
The guest warns that one bad specification line can produce tens of thousands of tokens of bad code and recommends reading specs before starting a serious run.
Back pressure is defined as executable feedback such as unit tests, builds, type checks, and security scans that can stop a bad generation.
The demonstrated prompt asks the agent to implement one highest priority feature, pass tests and linting, update the implementation plan, and commit.
Doing one item and exiting is presented as a way to keep each run in the useful portion of the context window.
Reverse mode reads an existing system to produce specifications that can later drive a forward implementation.
The loop is committed after each successful compilation so work can be rolled back to a known good point.
